name: CARE

paper.title: Conflict-Aware Soft Prompting for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

construction.unit: 16 soft context embeddings for one retrieved passage, encoded together with the question
construction.processing: context assessor (base LLM + LoRA) reads 'Question + Document' with 16 memory tokens; their last hidden states, passed through an MLP projector in the code, replace the passage in the prompt
construction.writer: context assessor: the base LLM with LoRA, trained by reconstruction pretraining then conflict-aware fine-tuning

organization.structure: static passage corpus (Wikipedia); no memory kept between questions
organization.stores: Wikipedia passages (Dec 2021 dump per the README)

management.conflicts: context-memory conflict handled inside the embeddings: trained to carry low reliability for passages that would mislead, so the LLM relies on its parametric knowledge

retrieval.selection: top-1 passage (top-3 in one extra test)

use.context: instruction + 'Background:' 16 projected embeddings + question, then 'The answer is:'
use.reasoning: single greedy generation by the frozen base LLM, at most 30 new tokens

classify.note: Retrieval is plain ColBERTv2 top-1; the contribution is how that one passage is encoded (16 soft embeddings trained to signal reliability), not which passage is chosen.

stages.construction: For each question the top-1 passage is written as 'Question: q / Document: passage', cut to 180 tokens, and encoded by the context assessor (base LLM + LoRA) with 16 memory tokens; the last-layer states at those tokens (through an MLP projector in the code) are the soft context embeddings.
stages.retrieval: ColBERTv2 retrieves the top-1 Wikipedia passage for the question.
stages.answer: The frozen base LLM gets the instruction, the 16 embeddings in place of the background passage and the question, and generates up to 30 tokens greedily.
stages.learning: The assessor is pretrained to reconstruct 2M Wikipedia passages from its embeddings, then fine-tuned on NQ: questions the LLM answers closed-book get a hard-negative passage and a no-context teacher, the rest get a passage containing the answer and a teacher reading it; loss is LM plus λ-weighted KL to the teacher. The base LLM is never updated.

summary: Encodes each retrieved passage with the question into 16 soft embeddings via a LoRA copy of the LLM, trained with helpful and hard-negative passages so the embeddings tell the frozen LLM how much to trust the passage.
notes: Venue: EMNLP 2025 main conference, ACL Anthology 2025.emnlp-main.1371 (pages 26981-26995); arXiv comment 'Accepted to EMNLP 2025'. Code github.com/eunseongc/CARE at ccb5fe49 (2025-10-23); evaluation data checked on Hugging Face eunseong/data_care (eval/nq/retrieval/colbertv2/test_question_aware.jsonl stores each passage as 'Question: ... Document: ...'). Text read from arXiv v2 PDF with pdftotext. The paper's context assessor is built on ICAE-style memory tokens (the code package is named ICAE) and xRAG's pretraining prompts.

sources.code_note: Latest commit (2025-10-23), after the camera-ready. It has pretraining, fine-tuning and evaluation scripts for Mistral, LLaMA and Qwen, and the data preparation notebook; released checkpoints are on Hugging Face. No retrieval code: ColBERTv2 results are shipped as data files.

headline: The memory is not a store: each retrieved passage is re-encoded with its question into 16 soft embeddings that take the passage's place in the prompt.
Conflict handling is learned, not decided: there is no gate; the embeddings are trained to be weak when the passage would mislead, and the frozen LLM then leans on what it knows.
All main tests use the single top-1 ColBERTv2 passage and short greedy answers (at most 30 tokens).

open_questions: No run isolates the conflict-aware training from compressing the passage into 16 embeddings: there is no plain soft-prompt baseline (for example the pretrained assessor alone) evaluated against RAG on the test sets.
Fine-tuning uses only NQ, so the three open-domain QA sets are close to the training task; on the out-of-domain TruthfulQA and FactKG, CARE is within 0.002 of RAG with Mistral.

glance.a: Nothing persistent. A static Wikipedia corpus is searched with ColBERTv2; the passage found is turned into 16 soft embeddings for this question only.

glance.q: Does the question shape the encoding?
glance.a: Yes. The assessor reads 'Question: … Document: …', so the same passage is encoded differently for different questions.

glance.q: Who decides to ignore a bad passage?
glance.a: No explicit decision. The embeddings are trained to carry less influence for misleading passages; the frozen LLM does the rest.

glance.q: What does the answer model read?
glance.a: An instruction, 16 embeddings where the passage would be, and the question. Never the passage text.

discussion.takeaway: Instead of deciding whether to trust a retrieved passage, CARE compresses it into a few soft embeddings trained to carry that trust, so a frozen LLM can ignore misleading context yet still use helpful context. It beats RAG and other conflict methods on average without fine-tuning the LLM.

claims.claim: Best average among methods that leave the LLM unchanged.
claims.evidence: Average 0.458 vs 0.436 RAG and 0.435 Priori Judgment (Mistral); 0.467 vs 0.440 and 0.453 (LLaMA). Table 2, §5.1.

claims.claim: Fine-tuning the LLM itself hurts other tasks.
claims.evidence: Direct FT and RetRobust drop on TruthfulQA (Mistral F1 0.102 / 0.152 vs CARE 0.279) and Direct FT on FactKG with LLaMA (0.305). Table 2.

claims.claim: Soft reliance beats a hard retrieve-or-not decision.
claims.evidence: With Mistral, +5.29% over the best adaptive-retrieval baseline (Priori Judgment 0.435 vs 0.458); Adaptive-RAG averages 0.427. §5.1, Table 2.

claims.claim: Both kinds of supervision are needed, and pretraining is essential.
claims.evidence: Positives only: Resilience 0.696; negatives only: Boost 0.071; no pretraining: 0.347 vs 0.438 overall. Table 3.
1.19 s per query vs 1.07 s RAG and 2.10 s Priori Judgment. Table 4.

claims.claim: Carries over to another LLM and to three passages.
claims.evidence: Qwen3-8B 0.454 vs 0.425 RAG (Table 7); top-3 NQ 0.504 vs 0.481 (Table 8).

limits: Only the top-1 passage and single-step answering are studied; conflicts among passages and within reasoning are left out (top-3 is a preliminary test).
A fixed budget of 16 embeddings suits short Wikipedia passages but may be too small for longer contexts.
Closed-book correctness is a noisy proxy for whether the LLM knows the answer.
reading: There is no persistent memory: the corpus is fixed and the soft context is rebuilt per question, so CARE is a way of reading retrieved evidence rather than of storing it.
The assessor sees the question with the passage (eq. 4; the released test file prefixes every passage with its question), so the same passage gets different embeddings for different questions.
Training uses NQ only. Gains are largest on the open-domain QA sets; with Mistral, CARE is 0.638 vs 0.639 for RAG on FactKG and 0.279 vs 0.277 F1 on TruthfulQA.
With LLaMA on WebQA the closed-book model (0.465) beats every retrieval method, CARE included (0.445).
All runs use a single seed (App. A.1), and several baselines were adapted (Adaptive-RAG relabelled to a binary retrieve decision, Priori Judgment used in its RAG setting; App. A.3).

abstract.text: When a retrieved passage contradicts what an LLM already knows correctly, standard RAG tends to follow the passage and get the answer wrong. CARE adds a context assessor, a LoRA-tuned copy of the base LLM that turns the question and passage into a few soft memory embeddings placed in the prompt instead of the passage. The assessor is first pretrained to reconstruct passages, then fine-tuned with helpful passages for questions the LLM cannot answer alone and hard negatives for questions it can, so the embeddings learn to signal how far to trust the passage. The base LLM is never fine-tuned, and CARE improves average results by about 5% over RAG across QA and fact-checking benchmarks.
